Summary: Adoptionism taught in the 2nd and 8th centuries that Jesus was born a human and was adopted as God's Son at his baptism or resurrection because of his obedience. It denied his pre-existence as God the Son.
Beliefs: Jesus was adopted as Son at his baptism; Jesus did not pre-exist as God; Jesus earned sonship by obedience; Christ's deity is a conferred status, not his nature
Controversy: Condemned in Rome in the late 2nd century and again in the Spanish Adoptionist controversy addressed at Frankfurt AD 794
ChristianResponse: The church affirmed that Jesus is God's Son by nature from eternity, citing John 1:1-14 and Romans 1:3-4.
